aaronite.label: Aaronite
aaronite.summary: Member of the hereditary priestly caste descended from Aaron, in the biblical tradition.
aaronite.text: A biblical term for the descendants of Aaron, brother of Moses, who formed the hereditary priestly caste of Israel (the kohanim) responsible for Temple service. In genealogical or religious texts of biblical inspiration, the word denotes a priestly lineage rather than an occupation in the strict sense.

abaiseur.label: Abaiseur (flattener)
abaiseur.summary: Craftsman specialized in a flattening technique applied to some material.
abaiseur.text: The term denotes a craftsman responsible for flattening a material (dough, metal, or leather, depending on the trade), a common operation in several traditional crafts. The precise meaning varies according to the trade context in which it appears in the record.

abat_faim.label: Abat-faim
abat_faim.summary: A hearty dish served at the start of a meal, or by extension an innkeeper serving copious food.
abat_faim.text: Literally "that which knocks down hunger", the term originally denoted a substantial dish served at the start of a meal to blunt the appetite before finer courses. By extension, it could describe the keeper of a cheap eating house serving copious food to workers.

abatis.label: Abatis
abatis.summary: Land-clearing work by felling and burning, notably in a colonial context.
abatis.text: In rural vocabulary, notably in New France and French Canada, "faire de l'abatis" meant clearing a plot of land by felling trees followed by burning, the first step in bringing new land under cultivation. The term could also denote the trade in offal and by-products of livestock slaughter, depending on context.

abatteur.label: Abatteur (coal-face miner)
abatteur.summary: Miner specialized in cutting coal or ore at the coal face.
abatteur.text: The abatteur is the underground miner responsible for detaching coal or ore from the seam, using a pick and later explosives or a pneumatic drill, in underground cutting workings. One of the most arduous and best-paid posts in the mining hierarchy, distinct from the timberman who shores up the gallery or the tram-pusher who hauls away the cut coal.

abatteur_de_besognes.label: Abatteur de besognes
abatteur_de_besognes.summary: Expression for a particularly fast and productive worker.
abatteur_de_besognes.text: "Abattre de la besogne" is an attested French expression meaning to get through a great deal of work in a short time. Used as an occupational descriptor, it denotes a worker known for his output and his ability to dispatch tasks quickly, rather than a defined profession as such.

abbe.label: Abbé (abbot)
abbe.summary: Title of the head of an abbey, or more broadly of a secular priest.
abbe.text: The abbé was originally the elected head of a monastic community (an abbey), responsible for directing its spiritual and temporal life. From the 17th century, the title also became a general courtesy form of address for any secular priest or tonsured cleric, even without an actual abbatial charge, a usage frequent in civil and parish records.

abbesse.label: Abbesse (abbess)
abbesse.summary: Elected head of a women's religious community governing an abbey.
abbesse.text: The abbess governs an abbey of nuns, with spiritual and often extensive temporal authority over the community's property and religious women; some abbesses of great royal abbeys held near-seigneurial rank. "Abadesse" is an old spelling of the word, common in medieval and Ancien Régime records.

abecedaire.label: Abécédaire
abecedaire.summary: Teacher responsible for teaching children the rudiments of reading and the alphabet.
abecedaire.text: The term denotes an elementary-level teacher responsible for teaching young children the alphabet and the first rudiments of reading with the aid of an abécédaire (a primer for learning letters). The term "ABC", sometimes recorded on its own in records as a job title, refers to the same basic instruction, a rung below the proper schoolmaster.

abergeur.label: Abergeur
abergeur.summary: Innkeeper lodging travelers, a term sometimes linked to land-lease charters.
abergeur.text: In its most common sense, the abergeur keeps an inn and lodges travelers, an old form of the word "aubergiste" (innkeeper). In some regions of southern France, the related word "albergement" also denoted a feudal or emphyteutic lease granting land; the exact meaning therefore depends on the context of the record.

aboyeur.label: Aboyeur (theatre barker)
aboyeur.summary: Barker posted at the entrance of a show, calling for carriages and alerting their owners.
aboyeur.text: The aboyeur stood at the door of theatres and shows to loudly hail coachmen and bring up spectators' carriages as they left. By extension, the word was also used for any barker haranguing the public in front of a fairground booth or a commercial establishment.

accordeur.label: Accordeur (tuner)
accordeur.summary: Craftsman specialized in tuning musical instruments.
accordeur.text: The accordeur is a craftsman specialized in tuning musical instruments, notably the organ, harpsichord, piano and harp. The trade requires a trained ear and a fine knowledge of instrument-making, and became a distinct profession with the spread of the piano in the 19th century.

accoucheuse.label: Accoucheuse (midwife)
accoucheuse.summary: Experienced woman assisting women in labour during childbirth.
accoucheuse.text: The accoucheuse, or midwife, assists women giving birth. Before the trade's official regulation and medical training in the 18th-19th centuries, the role was often practised empirically, passed down from mother to daughter in some families or recognized purely on the basis of experience.

accrocheur.label: Accrocheur (mine coupler)
accrocheur.summary: Miner responsible for coupling and handling tubs in underground galleries.
accrocheur.text: The accrocheur is the underground worker responsible for coupling coal tubs to haulage cables or trains, notably at the foot of the extraction shaft. A key post in the coal-evacuation chain, distinct from the abatteur who cuts the coal.

acheteur_de_bois_chantant.label: Acheteur de bois chantant
acheteur_de_bois_chantant.summary: Merchant selecting resonance wood with the acoustic qualities sought by instrument-makers.
acheteur_de_bois_chantant.text: The acheteur de bois chantant is a merchant or intermediary specialized in selecting and buying "singing wood" (notably spruce), chosen for its exceptional acoustic qualities and destined for luthiers making violins, cellos and other stringed instruments.

aciron.label: Aciron
aciron.text: According to the reference glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres, the aciron is a metalworker, a term linked to the working of iron and steel. The word remains rare and poorly documented beyond this general indication.

acolythe.label: Acolyte
acolythe.summary: Minor cleric assisting the priest during religious ceremonies.
acolythe.text: The acolyte is a cleric who has received one of the minor orders of the Catholic Church, responsible for assisting the celebrant during Mass and liturgical ceremonies (carrying torches, cruets). The order long formed a stage on the path toward the priesthood.

administrateur.label: Administrateur (administrator)
administrateur.summary: Person responsible for managing the affairs of a business, institution or estate.
administrateur.text: The administrateur runs or manages the day-to-day affairs of a business, public establishment, association or estate, ensuring its proper administrative and financial functioning. A very general term covering widely varying realities depending on the period and sector.

administrateur_des_colonies.label: Administrateur des colonies (colonial administrator)
administrateur_des_colonies.summary: Official responsible for the administrative management of a French colonial territory.
administrateur_des_colonies.text: The administrateur des colonies is an official of the French colonial civil service responsible for managing an overseas territory on the State's behalf, in administrative, judicial and economic matters. This corps existed from the 19th century until decolonization, trained notably at the École coloniale in Paris.

admodiateur.label: Admodiateur (leaseholder)
admodiateur.summary: Manager responsible, for a fee, for operating land or property belonging to others.
admodiateur.text: The admodiateur leases ("admodiation") the operation of an estate, notably royal, seigneurial or ecclesiastical, in exchange for a fixed fee paid to the owner, then drawing the operating income for his own profit. The term is close to that of tax farmer but usually applies to smaller holdings.

adoubeur_de_corps_humain.label: Adoubeur de corps humain
adoubeur_de_corps_humain.summary: Enigmatic term evoking body care or funerary practices.
adoubeur_de_corps_humain.text: The verb "adouber" originally meant to equip or arm (notably a knight), before taking on the more general sense of arranging or preparing. Applied to the "human body", the term might denote an activity of body care, of a bonesetter, or of preparing bodies for burial, but its precise meaning is not clearly established.

affaneur.label: Affaneur
affaneur.summary: Agricultural day-labourer toiling at hard tasks, hired by the day.
affaneur.text: Formed on the old verb "affaner" (to toil, to work hard), the affaneur is an agricultural day-labourer hired by the task or by the day, owning neither land nor his own team of draught animals. The term is attested in Old French and in some southern dialects, where it denotes the plain field hand.

affeagiste.label: Afféagiste
affeagiste.summary: One who grants land under a perpetual feudal or emphyteutic lease.
affeagiste.text: The afféagiste is one who grants an "afféagement", a form of perpetual or very long-term lease granting the use of land (often seigneurial or communal) in exchange for an annual fee. This practice was notably used to develop salt marshes on the Atlantic coast and uncultivated land.

afficheur.label: Afficheur (bill poster)
afficheur.summary: Worker responsible for pasting up posters at authorized locations.
afficheur.text: The afficheur pastes up posters (official notices, advertisements, show programmes) on walls and public hoardings, often holding an authorization or a regulated status, since the posting of unauthorized bills was traditionally controlled by municipalities.

affineur.label: Affineur (refiner)
affineur.summary: Worker specialized in a refining operation, depending on the trade concerned.
affineur.text: The term "affineur" covers several trades depending on context: refining hemp for the ropemaker, refining precious metals for the metalworker or goldsmith, or refining cheeses. In rural records, it most often denotes the worker who prepares hemp or flax fibre for spinning.

affineur_d_or_et_d_argent.label: Affineur d'Or et d'Argent (gold and silver refiner)
affineur_d_or_et_d_argent.summary: Worker separating gold and silver and bringing them to the required degree of purity.
affineur_d_or_et_d_argent.text: The affineur d'or et d'argent separates the two precious metals, often naturally or deliberately alloyed together, and purifies them to the fineness required for their intended use (coinage, goldsmithing).

afforeur.label: Afforeur
afforeur.summary: Agent responsible for setting or collecting the aforage duty on goods sold.
afforeur.text: The afforeur is responsible for the "aforage" (or afforage), a duty or fee set on the measuring or retail sale of certain goods, particularly wine, before their public sale. The word also more broadly covers a function of assessing and taxing merchandise.

affranchisseur.label: Affranchisseur
affranchisseur.summary: One who frees, manumits, or grants an exemption, the exact meaning depending on the context of the record.
affranchisseur.text: "Affranchir" can mean granting freedom to a serf or slave, releasing someone from a due or a levy, or franking mail for postage, depending on the period of the record. "Affranchisseux" is a dialectal variant of the term.

affranchisseur_de_betail.label: Affranchisseur de bétail
affranchisseur_de_betail.summary: Presumably responsible for freeing livestock from certain seigneurial obligations or dues.
affranchisseur_de_betail.text: The term probably denotes a specialist responsible for freeing domestic animals from certain seigneurial obligations, tolls, or legal constraints on their ownership or movement, though the available source does not allow this hypothesis to be confirmed further.

afgiste.label: Afgiste
afgiste.summary: Copyist working in a scriptorium or a monastery of copyists.
afgiste.text: According to the glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres, the afgiste supposedly denotes a copyist working in a scriptorium or a monastery of copyists, responsible for reproducing manuscripts and documents before the invention of printing. The source is isolated and the term too rare to be considered fully established.

afoireur.label: Afoireur
afoireur.summary: Public crier announcing fairs and news in villages.
afoireur.text: Presumably formed on "foire" (fair), the term denotes a public crier responsible for announcing fairs, markets and important news in villages and towns, at a time when oral communication remained the chief means of spreading information in rural areas.

agent_a_gage.label: Agent à gage
agent_a_gage.summary: Employee receiving a guaranteed wage in exchange for specified services.
agent_a_gage.text: The agent à gage is an employee receiving a guaranteed wage, and often lodging, in exchange for specific services rendered to an employer. The term is opposed to piecework or day labour, which was more precarious.

agent_d_affaires.label: Agent d'affaires (business agent)
agent_d_affaires.summary: Professional responsible for managing a client's commercial, administrative or legal interests.
agent_d_affaires.text: The agent d'affaires is a professional responsible for managing the commercial, administrative or legal interests of clients: debt collection, property management, dealings with administrations. Little regulated before the 20th century, the trade resembled, depending on the case, that of a lawyer, broker, or private steward.

agent_de_remplacements_militaires.label: Agent de remplacements militaires
agent_de_remplacements_militaires.summary: Intermediary organizing, for payment, the replacement of a conscript for military service.
agent_de_remplacements_militaires.text: The agent de remplacements militaires is a specialized intermediary who organized, for a fee, replacement for military service on behalf of wealthy young men wishing to escape conscription. This "replacement" system, legal in France from the late 18th century until 1872, gave rise to a genuine market for substitutes, often decried for its social unfairness.

agent_des_impots.label: Agent des impôts (tax official)
agent_des_impots.summary: Official responsible for assessing, checking or collecting tax.
agent_des_impots.text: The agent des impôts is a tax-administration official responsible for assessing, checking or collecting taxes owed by taxpayers. The role and its organization varied greatly across successive tax regimes, from the Ancien Régime's tax farming to the modern public-finance administration.

agent_des_moeurs.label: Agent des mœurs (vice-squad officer)
agent_des_moeurs.summary: Police official responsible for monitoring behaviour deemed contrary to public morals.
agent_des_moeurs.text: The agent des mœurs is a police official specialized in monitoring and suppressing behaviour considered contrary to public morals, notably prostitution, whose regulation occupied a dedicated squad in large French cities in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

agent_voyer.label: Agent voyer
agent_voyer.summary: Technical official responsible for the upkeep and oversight of roads and lanes.
agent_voyer.text: The agent voyer is a technical official of the local roads service, created in the 19th century, responsible for building, maintaining and overseeing the roads, lanes and structures of a canton or district. The role prefigures the modern local highways corps.

ageyeur.label: Ageyeur (wire-drawing puller)
ageyeur.summary: Wire-drawing worker pulling wire through drawplates by hand.
ageyeur.text: The ageyeur is a specialized wire-drawing worker responsible for pulling iron wire through drawplates (perforated dies that size the wire) by main force, before this arduous operation was mechanized.

agioteur.label: Agioteur (speculator)
agioteur.summary: Speculator profiting from fluctuations in exchange rates and prices.
agioteur.text: The agioteur is a financial speculator who profits from fluctuations in rates, differences in exchange, and price variations between different markets ("agiotage"). The term, often pejorative, is particularly associated with speculators on assignats and state loans during the French Revolution.

agreministe.label: Agréministe
agreministe.summary: Maker and fitter of ornaments and trimmings for ceremonial garments.
agreministe.text: The agréministe makes and fits clothing ornaments ("agréments": braids, trimmings, embroidery) on gowns, ceremonial dress and ecclesiastical vestments, a trade close to passementerie and to the tailor of formal wear.

agriculteur.label: Agriculteur (farmer)
agriculteur.summary: Operator working the land to produce agricultural goods.
agriculteur.text: The agriculteur farms land, as owner, tenant farmer or sharecropper, to produce crops or raise livestock. The term, which appeared in the 18th century as a gradual replacement for "laboureur" and "cultivateur", became the standard administrative designation for the profession over the 19th and 20th centuries.

agrimandeur.label: Agrimandeur
agrimandeur.summary: Regional term for a surveyor, one who measures land.
agrimandeur.text: Under several regional spellings, the term denotes a surveyor or land measurer, responsible for assessing areas and marking out property boundaries, a function standard French more commonly designates by "arpenteur" or "agrimenseur".

aide_agriculteur.label: Aide-agriculteur (farmhand)
aide_agriculteur.summary: Worker assisting the farmer with farm work.
aide_agriculteur.text: The aide-agriculteur assists the operator with the routine work of the farm: ploughing, sowing, harvesting, livestock care, without bearing the responsibility of running the operation. The term denotes a farm employee rather than an operator in his own right.

aide_boiseur.label: Aide boiseur
aide_boiseur.summary: Young mine worker assisting the timberman in placing support props.
aide_boiseur.text: The aide boiseur assists the boiseur, the miner responsible for shoring up galleries with timber to prevent collapse. This post was often held by young miners starting their career underground, before moving on to more skilled positions such as coal-cutting.

aiguilletier.label: Aiguilletier (aglet-maker)
aiguilletier.summary: Craftsman making aiguillettes, metal-tipped laces used to fasten garments.
aiguilletier.text: The aiguilletier makes aiguillettes: cords or laces fitted with a metal tip (aglet) at each end, used before the button became widespread to fasten the various pieces of a garment. The trade, a distinct guild, should not be confused with the aiguillier, who makes sewing needles.

aiguilleur.label: Aiguilleur (railway signalman)
aiguilleur.summary: Employee responsible for operating railway points.
aiguilleur.text: The aiguilleur operates the controls of the points that switch trains from one track to another, a trade that appeared with the development of the railway in the 19th century and was essential to traffic safety before automation.

aiguillier.label: Aiguillier (needle-maker)
aiguillier.summary: Craftsman making sewing needles, knitting needles and other pointed tools.
aiguillier.text: The aiguillier makes sewing needles, knitting needles and other pointed tools used in textile crafts, a specialty close to that of the pin-maker. Some French towns, such as L'Aigle in Normandy, were renowned for this output from the 17th century onward.

aimetier.label: Aimétier
aimetier.text: The aimétier makes fish-hooks and other angling tackle, a precision craft working iron or steel wire, often based in towns close to river or sea fishing areas.

airier.label: Airier
airier.summary: Market gardener, grower of vegetables near towns.
airier.text: According to the glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres, the airier is a market gardener, a grower of vegetables for sale, the term probably relating to "aire" in the sense of a cultivated garden plot.

aixier.label: Aixier
aixier.summary: Joiner specialized in the interior ornamentation of major buildings.
aixier.text: The aixier is a joiner specialized in the interior ornamentation of public buildings and major constructions, a trade close to that of the ornamental joiner or cabinetmaker depending on the scale of the work undertaken.

ajoureuse.label: Ajoureuse (openwork embroiderer)
ajoureuse.summary: Female worker who adorns linen by drawing threads from the fabric to create decorative openwork.
ajoureuse.text: The ajoureuse embellishes shirts, tablecloths and household linen by withdrawing weft and warp threads in both directions, creating decorative openwork patterns, a technique close to drawn-thread hemstitching.

ajusteur.label: Ajusteur (fitter)
ajusteur.summary: Precision mechanic assembling and fine-tuning mechanical parts.
ajusteur.text: The ajusteur is a mechanic specialized in the precise fitting of mechanical parts, the assembly of complex units and the fine-tuning of devices requiring great precision. The trade developed with industrialization and is still used today in mechanical engineering and aeronautics.

alchimiste.label: Alchimiste (alchemist)
alchimiste.summary: Practitioner of alchemy, the discipline ancestral to modern chemistry.
alchimiste.text: The alchimiste practises alchemy, a discipline blending the quest for the transmutation of metals, occult philosophy and proto-chemical experimentation. Some alchemists enjoyed the protection of princely courts, while others practised on the margins, somewhere between scholar and charlatan depending on the period.

alenier.label: Alénier (awl-maker)
alenier.summary: Craftsman making awls and punches for working leather.
alenier.text: The alénier makes awls, the pointed punches used by shoemakers, saddlers and harness-makers to pierce leather before sewing it. Contrary to an etymology sometimes suggested through confusion with alum, the reference glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres confirms that "alainier", "aleinier" and "alleinier" are simply spelling variants of "alénier", not a distinct trade linked to the alum trade.

alerresse.label: Alerresse
alerresse.text: Attested in Middle French (15th century), the word "alerresse" denotes a midwife. It derives from the Latin "alitrix" ("nurse"), from the same family as the verb "alere", to nourish.

alfatier.label: Alfatier
alfatier.summary: Worker harvesting esparto grass, used in basketry and papermaking.
alfatier.text: The alfatier harvests esparto grass, a grass growing notably in North Africa, used to make ropes, mats and basketware, then widely used as a raw material in the paper industry from the 19th century onward.

alibastreur.label: Alibastreur
alibastreur.summary: Craftsman working alabaster for decorative sculpture and liturgical objects.
alibastreur.text: The alibastreur is a craftsman specialized in working alabaster, a fine translucent stone used for decorative sculpture, liturgical objects and certain architectural elements, notably in regions with quarries of this soft stone.

alleutier.label: Alleutier (allodial landholder)
alleutier.summary: Holder of land held in allod, free of any feudal charge.
alleutier.text: The alleutier farms land held in allod, that is, full and free property, not subject to the dues and obligations of feudal tenure. This status of free ownership, more common in the south of France, contrasted with censive or fief tenure.

allumettier.label: Allumettier (matchmaker)
allumettier.text: The allumettier is a craftsman, and later a factory worker, specialized in making matches, the small flammable sticks used to light fires, an industry that developed into factories from the mid-19th century, not without health risks for the female workers exposed to phosphorus.

allumeur_de_reverberes.label: Allumeur de réverbères (lamplighter)
allumeur_de_reverberes.summary: Municipal employee responsible for lighting and extinguishing street lamps on a fixed schedule.
allumeur_de_reverberes.text: The allumeur de réverbères is a municipal employee responsible for lighting and extinguishing street lamps (oil, then gas) every day on a schedule set by the season. The trade disappeared with the electrification and automation of street lighting at the turn of the 20th century.

alpagatier.label: Alpagatier (espadrille-maker)
alpagatier.summary: Craftsman making alpargatas, shoes with braided rope soles.
alpagatier.text: The alpagatier makes alpargatas (espadrilles), shoes made of a cloth upper and a sole braided from rope or rush, a traditional product of southwestern France and the Basque Country.

alpagiste.label: Alpagiste
alpagiste.summary: Herder working a mountain alpine pasture.
alpagiste.text: The alpagiste works an alpage, a mountain pasture used for the summer transhumance of livestock, often linked to the seasonal cheese-making typical of Alpine regions.

amadoueur.label: Amadoueur (tinder-maker)
amadoueur.summary: Craftsman preparing tinder, a flammable substance derived from a fungus.
amadoueur.text: The amadoueur prepares tinder, a spongy substance obtained from the tinder fungus (a polypore), used before matches to catch fire thanks to its high flammability, notably with a flint-and-steel firestarter.

amidonier.label: Amidonier (starch-maker)
amidonier.text: The amidonier makes and sells starch, extracted notably from wheat, used in cooking, in laundering for stiffening linen, and in certain old pharmaceutical or cosmetic uses (powder for wigs).

amineur.label: Amineur
amineur.summary: Employee of salt warehouses responsible for measuring and distributing salt.
amineur.text: The amineur worked in the royal salt warehouses of the Ancien Régime, responsible for measuring and distributing salt by the minot, the unit of measure used under the gabelle, the royal tax on salt.

amman.label: Amman
amman.summary: Municipal magistrate of Germanic origin, the Alsatian equivalent of the bailiff or the mayor.
amman.text: The amman (from the German "Amtmann") is a municipal magistrate found in regions of Germanic tradition, notably Alsace, exercising administrative and judicial functions comparable to those of a bailli or a mayor in territories under French law.

amoulageur.label: Amoulageur (millwright)
amoulageur.summary: Carpenter specialized in building the wooden waterwheels and gearing of mills.
amoulageur.text: The amoulageur (or carpenter-amoulageur) builds the wooden waterwheels and gearing of watermills and windmills, a craft requiring cross-disciplinary skills in masonry, metalwork, hydraulics, mechanics, wheelwrighting and carpentry; each wheel requires 800 to 1,200 hours of bespoke work. Officially recognized among the building trades by the decree of 9 April 1936, the trade has become extremely rare: fewer than ten practitioners remained in France in 2007. According to some dictionaries, the term could also, in other regions, denote a simple grinder sharpening cutting tools on a wheel — hence the variants "amoulaire" and "amoulangeur".

amphibie.label: Amphibie
amphibie.summary: Print-shop worker combining the roles of typesetter and printer or proofreader.
amphibie.text: In the jargon of printing workshops, the "amphibie" denotes a typographer who works both as a typesetter and as a printer, or as a typesetter and a proofreader, thus combining two functions usually kept separate in the workshop.

ancele.label: Ancèle
ancele.summary: Female servant employed in domestic tasks in a house or estate.
ancele.text: From the Latin "ancilla" (female servant), the term denotes a female servant employed in houses and estates for various domestic tasks, an old word characteristic of medieval and Old French vocabulary.

anier.label: Ânier (donkey-driver)
anier.summary: Driver of donkeys used to transport loads.
anier.text: The ânier drives donkeys used to transport goods, particularly over difficult terrain (mountains, narrow paths) where these sturdy, undemanding animals excelled over the horse or mule.

annonceur.label: Annonceur (announcer)
annonceur.summary: Professional responsible for publicly broadcasting announcements and information.
annonceur.text: The annonceur is responsible for broadcasting announcements, news and important information to the public, a role close to that of the public crier in Ancien Régime society. In the 20th century the word took on the modern sense of an advertiser, a business or person that places advertising.

anseur_de_pots.label: Anseur de pots
anseur_de_pots.summary: Potter specialized in making and attaching handles to vessels.
anseur_de_pots.text: The anseur de pots is a potter specialized in making and attaching handles to ceramic vessels, an operation distinct from throwing the body of the pot, often carried out by a dedicated worker in large potteries.

anspessade.label: Anspessade
anspessade.summary: Junior military rank in the Ancien Régime infantry, below corporal.
anspessade.text: The anspessade (from the Italian "lancia spezzata", broken lance, denoting a seasoned soldier) is a junior military rank in the French Ancien Régime infantry, below corporal, granted to a private who had distinguished himself through seniority or conduct.

antiquaire.label: Antiquaire (antique dealer)
antiquaire.summary: Dealer in antiques and art objects.
antiquaire.text: The antiquaire trades in antiques, furniture, paintings and works of art, an activity that became a profession from the 19th century onward with the rise of the art market and a taste for antiquities.

anysetier.label: Anysetier
anysetier.summary: Maker or seller of aniseed-flavoured drinks and confectionery.
anysetier.text: The anysetier makes or sells aniseed-based drinks and confectionery, such as anisette or sugared almonds, a trade linked to the traditional flavouring of French liqueurs and sweets.

apiculteur.label: Apiculteur (beekeeper)
apiculteur.summary: Keeper of bees for the production of honey and wax.
apiculteur.text: The apiculteur keeps bees for the production of honey, wax and, more recently, royal jelly and propolis. The modern standard term, it gradually replaced older designations such as "abeillier". The term replaces older designations such as "abeillier" (who kept bees in woven-straw hives, notably for the wax of church candles before electrification) or its Occitan equivalent "abeilladou".

apieceur.label: Apiéceur (piece-worker)
apieceur.summary: Garment-industry worker paid by the piece rather than by time.
apieceur.text: The apiéceur works for a master tailor or a clothing workshop, paid "by the piece" for assembling or finishing garments, a common form of pay in the clothing industry before time-based wage labour became standard.

aplaigneur.label: Aplaigneur (leveller)
aplaigneur.summary: Craftsman specialized in levelling surfaces of wood, metal or other material.
aplaigneur.text: The aplaigneur is a craftsman specialized in levelling surfaces, particularly in working wood, metal or other materials requiring a perfectly smooth, even finish, a trade known under several closely related spellings (aplaneur, applaigneur).

aplanisseur.label: Aplanisseur (planisher)
aplanisseur.summary: Craftsman specialized in professionally smoothing and levelling surfaces.
aplanisseur.text: The aplanisseur masters the techniques of smoothing and levelling surfaces (metal, wood, leather) to achieve a perfectly flat finish, a common finishing operation in several metal and wood crafts.

aplanyeur_de_drap.label: Aplanyeur de drap
aplanyeur_de_drap.summary: Craftsman levelling woollen cloth to give it a smooth, even surface.
aplanyeur_de_drap.text: The aplanyeur de drap is a craftsman specialized in levelling woollen fabrics, particularly broadcloth, a finishing operation in the cloth trade intended to give the fabric a smooth, even surface before sale.

aplatisseur.label: Aplatisseur (flattener)
aplatisseur.summary: Craftsman reducing the thickness of various materials by flattening.
aplatisseur.text: The aplatisseur is a craftsman specialized in flattening various materials — metals, leathers, textiles — requiring a reduction in thickness or flattening, an operation carried out with a hammer, a rolling mill or a press depending on the material.

aplatisseur_de_corne.label: Aplatisseur de corne
aplatisseur_de_corne.summary: Craftsman turning animal horn into flat sheets for various objects.
aplatisseur_de_corne.text: The aplatisseur de corne turns animal horn, first softened by heat, into flat sheets used to make various objects: combs, buttons, tool handles, lanterns, an essential step in the craft of horn-working.

apothicaire.label: Apothicaire (apothecary)
apothicaire.summary: Old-time pharmacist preparing and selling remedies and medicines.
apothicaire.text: The apothicaire prepares and sells remedies, drugs and medicines, the ancestor of the modern pharmacist. A member of a guild regulated from the Middle Ages, he kept an open shop and often worked alongside the physician, who prescribed, and the surgeon, who operated.

appareilleur.label: Appareilleur (stone-setter)
appareilleur.summary: Building technician determining the cutting and arrangement of construction stones.
appareilleur.text: In building and stone-cutting, the appareilleur determines the "appareil", that is, the arrangement and cutting of the stones of a piece of masonry, drawing up execution plans from the architect's designs. The term has more broadly come to cover the preparation and ordering of complex technical elements in other trades.

appariteur.label: Appariteur (usher/beadle)
appariteur.summary: Junior official conveying the acts and summonses of a public authority.
appariteur.text: The appariteur is a junior official responsible for representing a public authority (court, university, administration), notably by conveying summonses, citations and official documents to the parties concerned.

appreciateur.label: Appréciateur (appraiser)
appreciateur.summary: Expert responsible for valuing various kinds of property.
appreciateur.text: The appréciateur is an expert specialized in valuing various kinds of property — furniture, real estate, goods, works of art — notably at probate, public sales or inventories, a role close to that of the modern auctioneer.

appreciateur_ordinaire_de_meubles.label: Appréciateur ordinaire de meubles
appreciateur_ordinaire_de_meubles.summary: Official expert specialized in valuing furniture.
appreciateur_ordinaire_de_meubles.text: The appréciateur ordinaire de meubles is an official expert specialized in valuing furniture, notably for probate inventories drawn up by a notary, a charge sometimes regulated and sworn depending on the jurisdiction.

apprenti_mineur.label: Apprenti mineur (apprentice miner)
apprenti_mineur.summary: Young worker beginning his training in mine work.
apprenti_mineur.text: The apprenti mineur is a young worker beginning his career underground, assigned simple, supervised tasks — haulage, minor timbering work, assisting skilled workers — before gradually moving on to more specialized posts such as coal-cutting.

appreteur_de_bas.label: Apprêteur de bas (stocking finisher)
appreteur_de_bas.summary: Craftsman specialized in finishing silk, wool or cotton stockings.
appreteur_de_bas.text: The apprêteur de bas is a craftsman specialized in finishing silk, wool or cotton stockings, a finishing step (smoothing, dyeing, shaping) carried out after knitting on a stocking frame.

appreteur_de_chales.label: Apprêteur de châles (shawl finisher)
appreteur_de_chales.summary: Craftsman specialized in finishing shawls, fine luxury fabrics.
appreteur_de_chales.text: The apprêteur de châles is a craftsman specialized in finishing shawls, fine luxury fabrics and accessories, an industry that was particularly flourishing in 19th-century France with the fashion for cashmere-style shawls.

appreteuse.label: Apprêteuse
appreteuse.summary: Female worker who assembles and provisionally glues the pieces of a shoe or a hat before stitching.
appreteuse.text: The apprêteuse assembles and provisionally glues the various pieces of a shoe before the stitcher sews them together, or assembles the elements of a hat on its frame; a preparatory step in the production chain.

arbaletier.label: Arbalétrier (crossbow-maker)
arbaletier.summary: Maker of crossbows, or soldier fighting with a crossbow.
arbaletier.text: The arbalétrier makes crossbows or fights using them as his main weapon, an important military role in the Middle Ages before firearms became widespread, later perpetuated in civilian shooting confraternities (crossbowmen's companies).

archer.label: Archer
archer.summary: Warrior fighting with a bow, or armed member of the town watch.
archer.text: The archer is first a warrior using the bow as his main weapon, a major role in medieval armies. From the Ancien Régime onward, the word also denoted an armed member of the watch or the maréchaussée responsible for keeping order, the bow having by then given way to other weapons while the corps kept its name.

archer_des_gabelles.label: Archer des gabelles
archer_des_gabelles.summary: Armed tax officer responsible for enforcing the salt tax.
archer_des_gabelles.text: The archer des gabelles is an armed tax officer responsible for enforcing the taxes on salt (the gabelle) and combating salt smuggling, very active in border areas between provinces with different tax regimes under the Ancien Régime.

archetier.label: Archetier (bow-maker)
archetier.summary: Craftsman making bows for bowed string instruments.
archetier.text: The archetier makes bows for bowed string instruments: violins, violas, cellos, double basses. This precision trade, distinct from lutherie proper, requires specific skill in choosing the wood (notably pernambuco) and mounting the horsehair.

architecte.label: Architecte (architect)
architecte.summary: Professional designing and overseeing the construction of buildings.
architecte.text: The architecte designs the plans for a building and oversees its construction, attending to the function, soundness and aesthetics of the work. The profession became gradually regulated from the 19th century onward, up to today's requirement of a diploma and registration with the professional order of architects.

archiviste.label: Archiviste (archivist)
archiviste.summary: Professional responsible for preserving, classifying and providing access to archives.
archiviste.text: The archiviste preserves, classifies and makes accessible documents and archives, whether public (State archives, municipal archives) or private (business or family archives). In France, the archivists' profession took shape from the 19th century onward, notably with the founding of the École des chartes.

arconnier.label: Arçonnier (saddle-tree maker)
arconnier.summary: Craftsman making saddle-trees, the wooden frames of horse saddles.
arconnier.text: The arçonnier makes saddle-trees, curved wooden structures forming the frame of a horse saddle, onto which the saddler then fixes the leather and fittings. The trade is attested under many regional and older spellings (arçoneor, arçonier, arconneur, arcounier).

arctier.label: Arctier (bow and arrow maker)
arctier.text: The arctier makes bows and arrows, a craftsman specialized in projectile weapons, an important trade as long as archery and crossbow-shooting remained common weapons of war and hunting.

ardoisier.label: Ardoisier (slate worker)
ardoisier.summary: Craftsman quarrying, cutting and laying slate.
ardoisier.text: The ardoisier is specialized in quarrying, cutting and laying slate, a traditional roofing material in many French regions (Anjou, the Ardennes, Brittany), the term able to denote either the quarryman or the roofer depending on context.

arganpiere.label: Arganpière
arganpiere.text: According to the glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres, the arganpière is a female worker who hand-braids made-to-measure crinolines (the hooped-skirt frames worn in the 19th century), a specialized textile craft linked to the women's fashion of the time.

argousin.label: Argousin
argousin.summary: Junior officer guarding convicts chained on the royal galleys.
argousin.text: The argousin is a junior officer on the royal galleys, responsible for guarding and making the convicts chained to the oars work. The term later took on, by pejorative extension, the colloquial sense of a policeman or an overzealous guard.

armailler.label: Armailler
armailler.summary: Mountain cowherd tending herds and making cheese on alpine pastures.
armailler.text: The armailler tends and drives cows on alpine pastures, notably in the Jura, Franche-Comté and regions with a Gruyère-style cheesemaking tradition, where he also makes the cheese during the summer grazing season. A related spelling, "almailler", is also attested.

armurier.label: Armurier (armourer)
armurier.summary: Craftsman making, repairing and maintaining weapons of war and of the hunt.
armurier.text: The armurier makes, repairs and maintains weapons of war and of the hunt: edged weapons originally, then firearms once they spread. The trade is still practised today, notably for hunting and collector's firearms.

armurier_de_mains.label: Armurier de mains
armurier_de_mains.summary: Armourer specialized in making gauntlets and armoured gloves.
armurier_de_mains.text: The armurier de mains is an armourer specialized in making gauntlets and armoured gloves, a sub-specialty of medieval and Renaissance armour-making devoted to the articulated protection of a combatant's hands.

arnesaire.label: Arnesaire
arnesaire.summary: Occitan harness-maker producing harnesses and equipment for horses.
arnesaire.text: The arnesaire is a harness-maker, collar-maker, saddler and coachbuilder in Occitania, making harnesses and equipment for horses. In the Toulouse area, this same trade was sometimes called by the regional variant "arnesié".

arnezier.label: Arnezier
arnezier.summary: Farmer of Haute-Garonne ploughing with a traditional plough called an arnez.
arnezier.text: The arnezier is a farmer of Haute-Garonne who ploughs with an "arnez", a kind of traditional plough or ard specific to this region, the term denoting the tool rather than a trade distinct from that of the ploughman.

arpenteur.label: Arpenteur (surveyor)
arpenteur.summary: Expert in land measurement, responsible for marking out properties and areas.
arpenteur.text: The arpenteur is a land-measurement expert responsible for marking out properties, calculating areas and drawing up land plans, using local units of measure (the arpent) before metric unification. His surveys served as the basis for land transactions and tax assessments.

arpenteur_du_prince.label: Arpenteur du prince
arpenteur_du_prince.summary: Official surveyor in the service of royal or princely power.
arpenteur_du_prince.text: The arpenteur du prince is an official surveyor in the service of royal or princely power, responsible notably for measuring and marking out the land of the sovereign's domain, with greater authority and standing than a private surveyor.

arquebusier.label: Arquebusier
arquebusier.summary: Soldier armed with an arquebus, or craftsman making them.
arquebusier.text: The arquebusier is a soldier armed with an arquebus, one of the first portable firearms, which appeared in the 15th century and was used until the musket became standard. The word also denotes the craftsman who makes these weapons.

arracheur.label: Arracheur (puller)
arracheur.summary: Worker specialized in pulling up or out various materials, depending on context.
arracheur.text: The arracheur is a worker specialized in pulling up or extracting various things — plants, roots, stakes, nails — depending on the trade or the agricultural or craft context to which he is attached in the record.

arracheur_de_dents.label: Arracheur de dents (tooth-puller)
arracheur_de_dents.summary: Itinerant practitioner specialized in tooth extraction, before the emergence of the dentist.
arracheur_de_dents.text: The arracheur de dents is an often itinerant practitioner specialized in tooth extraction, relieving dental suffering by pulling diseased teeth, sometimes at fairs and markets. He preceded the emergence of the qualified, regulated dentist in the 19th century.

arricandier.label: Arricandier
arricandier.summary: Worker responsible for earthworks and carrying stone in quarries.
arricandier.text: The arricandier is a worker responsible for earthworks and carrying stone in quarries, a manual and arduous role essential to quarry operations before mechanization.

arrimeur.label: Arrimeur (stevedore)
arrimeur.summary: Specialist in loading and stowing cargo aboard ships.
arrimeur.text: The arrimeur is a specialist in loading and stowing ships, responsible for arranging the cargo optimally to ensure the ship's stability and the safety of the goods during the voyage.

arrondisseur.label: Arrondisseur
arrondisseur.summary: Craftsman specialized in giving various materials a rounded shape.
arrondisseur.text: The arrondisseur is a craftsman specialized in giving various materials — wood, metal, stone — a rounded shape, a finishing operation found in several material-working trades.

arroseur_public.label: Arroseur public
arroseur_public.summary: Municipal employee responsible for watering streets and public spaces.
arroseur_public.text: The arroseur public is a municipal employee responsible for watering streets, squares and public spaces to lay the dust, cool the air and keep the town clean, a common role before the widespread paving of roads.

arsonnier.label: Arsonnier
arsonnier.summary: Carder working textile fibres with the bow-shaped carding tool.
arsonnier.text: The arsonnier is a carder, a craftsman specialized in carding textile fibres (notably wool) with the "arçon", a vibrating-string tool that teased apart and aerated the fibre before spinning.

artilleur.label: Artilleur (artilleryman)
artilleur.summary: Soldier serving cannon and artillery pieces.
artilleur.text: The artilleur serves cannon and artillery pieces, a military arm whose importance grew steadily from the late Middle Ages until it became decisive in modern conflicts.

artiste.label: Artiste
artiste.summary: Creator of works with an aesthetic purpose: painting, sculpture, music, performance.
artiste.text: The artiste is a creator specialized in producing works with an aesthetic purpose: painting, sculpture, music, literature, theatre. A very general term, often used in civil records without further precision to denote a person practising an artistic or performing trade.

artiste_en_cheveux.label: Artiste en Cheveux (hair artist)
artiste_en_cheveux.summary: Artist creating decorative pictures (portraits, landscapes) out of braided hair.
artiste_en_cheveux.text: The artiste en cheveux made, chiefly in the 19th century, decorative pictures depicting portraits, landscapes or still lifes composed of braided and worked hair, often as a keepsake for a deceased person or a loved one.

artiste_mecanicien.label: Artiste Mécanicien
artiste_mecanicien.summary: Technician responsible for making, maintaining and improving the machines of a mint.
artiste_mecanicien.text: The artiste mécanicien is a specialized technician responsible for making, maintaining and improving the machines used in mints.

artiste_veterinaire.label: Artiste vétérinaire
artiste_veterinaire.summary: Veterinarian treating performance or circus animals.
artiste_veterinaire.text: The term seems to denote a veterinarian specialized in caring for performance animals (circus, menagerie, trained animals), combining ordinary veterinary practice with familiarity with the world of entertainment, though this designation does not correspond to an officially recognized title.

ascensionniste.label: Ascensionniste
ascensionniste.summary: Mountaineer or aeronaut who climbs mountains or makes balloon ascents.
ascensionniste.text: The ascensionniste makes ascents, whether in the mountains (mountaineering, before the modern term became widespread) or by balloon (ballooning), an activity of exploration and sometimes of spectacle very much in vogue in the 18th and 19th centuries.

aspleuse.label: Aspleuse
aspleuse.summary: Belgian mill worker responsible for setting the threads on the looms.
aspleuse.text: According to the glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres, the aspleuse is, in Belgium, a female spinning-mill worker responsible for setting the threads on the looms before or during spinning.

assecheur_de_marais.label: Assécheur de marais (marsh drainer)
assecheur_de_marais.summary: Specialist in hydraulic drainage, turning marshland into farmland.
assecheur_de_marais.text: The assécheur de marais masters the hydraulic drainage techniques needed to turn marshland into usable farmland, expertise particularly called upon in France from the 17th century onward, notably with the use of Dutch engineers to drain coastal marshes such as the Marais Poitevin.

asseeurs.label: Asséeurs
asseeurs.summary: Local officials responsible for apportioning the taille tax among taxpayers.
asseeurs.text: The asséeurs are responsible for the "assiette" (apportionment) of the taille, the royal direct tax, among the inhabitants of a parish, a task distinct from that of the collectors, who then carried out the actual collection of the sums owed.

assistant.label: Assistant
assistant.summary: Person helping a professional or a team in carrying out their duties.
assistant.text: The assistant supports a professional or a team in carrying out their duties, a generic term whose precise content depends entirely on the trade or sector to which it is attached in the record.

astrologue.label: Astrologue (astrologer)
astrologue.summary: Practitioner of astrology, interpreting the influence of the stars on events.
astrologue.text: The astrologue practises astrology, a discipline aiming to interpret the supposed influence of the stars on earthly events and individual fate, an activity that long stood alongside learned astronomy before the two definitively separated in the modern era.

atacheeur.label: Atacheeur
atacheeur.summary: Maker of small nails used to fix trimmings on belts.
atacheeur.text: According to the glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres, the atacheeur (or attachier) makes small nails used to fix trimmings on belts, a small-hardware craft linked to leatherworking and clothing.

atournaresse.label: Atournaresse
atournaresse.summary: Woman whose trade was to dress the hair of, adorn and dress women for a ceremony.
atournaresse.text: The atournaresse made a trade of dressing hair, adorning, and hiring out jewels for women attending a ceremony or celebration, notably a wedding. Jean Nicot's Thresor de la langue françoise (1606) attests the variant "achemeresse" as an exact synonym, linking it to the "Dames" or "Damoiselles d'atour" who filled a comparable office for princesses.

attacheuse.label: Attacheuse
attacheuse.summary: Silk-mill worker responsible for attaching the cords used on looms.
attacheuse.text: The attacheuse works in a silk mill where she is responsible for attaching the cords (codages) used to operate the looms, notably Jacquard looms.

aubergiste.label: Aubergiste (innkeeper)
aubergiste.summary: Keeper of an inn, lodging and feeding travellers.
aubergiste.text: The aubergiste keeps an inn, an establishment offering lodging and meals to travellers. Very common along post roads and pilgrimage routes, the trade was often regulated by guilds and monitored by the authorities to police travelling strangers.

auffier.label: Auffier
auffier.summary: Maker of ropes and nets on the Mediterranean coast.
auffier.text: According to the glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres, the auffier is, on the Mediterranean coast, a maker of ropes and nets, a craft linked to fishing and seafaring, distinct from the aulphier/auphier, who works with willow.

aulmucier.label: Aulmucier
aulmucier.summary: Maker of amices, fur headwear worn by canons.
aulmucier.text: The aulmucier makes amices, fur-lined liturgical headwear worn notably by canons during services, a specialized craft of ecclesiastical furriery attested under several spellings (aumucier, aumussier).

auneur.label: Auneur (aulnager)
auneur.summary: Official measurer of cloth sold by the ell.
auneur.text: The auneur measures and checks the length of fabric sold by the aune (ell), an old unit of length in the textile trade, a function often regulated and sworn to guarantee fair dealing.

auneur_jure.label: Auneur juré (sworn aulnager)
auneur_jure.summary: Cloth measurer officially sworn in by the authorities.
auneur_jure.text: The auneur juré is an auneur officially sworn in, vested by the municipal or guild authorities with a duty to check the measuring and sale of fabric, guaranteeing fair commercial dealing.

auvergneur.label: Auvergneur
auvergneur.summary: Term linked to migrants from the Auvergne, often coal or water merchants in Paris.
auvergneur.text: The term relates to the major migration of Auvergnats to Paris and other large cities in the 19th and 20th centuries, where they specialized notably in the coal and firewood trade (the "bougnats"), water-carrying and catering, going on to found many of Paris's café-tabac-coal shops.

avaleur_de_nefs.label: Avaleur de nefs
avaleur_de_nefs.summary: River pilot guiding boats through the difficult stretches of the Seine at Paris.
avaleur_de_nefs.text: The avaleur de nefs is a river pilot specialized in steering boats through the dangerous stretches of the Seine as it crosses Paris (eddies, floods, narrow bridge arches), using ropes, poles and a small boat called a "flette". The office was regulated by an ordinance of the provost of the Paris merchants as early as 1416; these pilots, paid per passage, also collected tolls proportional to the goods carried, until the office was abolished in 1854.

avaleur_de_vin.label: Avaleur de vin
avaleur_de_vin.summary: Handler responsible for lowering and rolling wine casks into a cellar.
avaleur_de_vin.text: According to the glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres, the avaleur de vin is a handler responsible for lowering and rolling wine casks, notably for cellaring, the verb "avaler" being used here in its old sense of "to bring down".

avenier.label: Avenier
avenier.text: The avenier trades in oats, a grain essential to feeding horses, an indispensable activity as long as animal traction dominated transport and farm work.

avitailleur.label: Avitailleur (victualler)
avitailleur.summary: Person responsible for supplying and provisioning, notably ships.
avitailleur.text: The avitailleur handles the supplying and provisioning of food, water or fuel, historically for ships in port, a function still in use today to denote the supplying of ships and aircraft.

bachelier.label: Bachelier
bachelier.summary: Social and feudal status denoting a young noble not yet a knight banneret.
bachelier.text: In feudal society, the bachelier is a young noble who has received the knightly accolade but does not yet have his own banner or a fief large enough to raise his own men, an intermediate status between squire and knight banneret. Within guilds the word also denoted an intermediate status between apprentice and master.

bachoteur.label: Bachoteur
bachoteur.summary: Boatman ferrying passengers or goods with a flat-bottomed skiff.
bachoteur.text: The bachoteur is a boatman using a "bachot", a small flat-bottomed boat, to ferry across a river, carry light goods, or fish on rivers and ponds.

baconnier.label: Baconnier
baconnier.summary: Maker or seller of bacon and salted pork.
baconnier.text: The baconnier makes or sells bacon and salted pork, a charcuterie activity linked to preserving meat before the spread of industrial refrigeration.

badestamier.label: Badestamier
badestamier.summary: Hosier making stockings from estame, a coarse combed wool.
badestamier.text: The badestamier is a hosier making stockings from estame, a coarse combed wool that is spun and then knitted, a specialty of woollen hosiery distinct from finer silk hosiery.

badigeonneur.label: Badigeonneur (whitewasher)
badigeonneur.summary: House painter applying plaster, whitewash and distemper to walls.
badigeonneur.text: The badigeonneur is a house painter specialized in applying renders, whitewash, paint or distemper to façades and interior walls, a common finishing trade before the spread of modern paints.

bagnard.label: Bagnard (convict)
bagnard.summary: Prisoner sentenced to forced labour in a penal colony.
bagnard.text: The bagnard is a prisoner sentenced to forced labour, serving his sentence in a bagne — on the galleys and then in the naval ports (Toulon, Brest, Rochefort) before the creation of the colonial penal colonies of French Guiana and New Caledonia in the 19th century.

bagotier.label: Bagotier
bagotier.text: The bagotier is a day-labourer doing temporary, seasonal work as needed by employers, a regional term for casual, unskilled labour.

bagottier.label: Bagottier (railway porter)
bagottier.summary: Porter carrying luggage at a railway station for travellers.
bagottier.text: The bagottier is a luggage porter at a railway station, responsible for carrying and handling travellers' luggage, a role that appeared with the development of the railway and large urban stations.

bahutier.label: Bahutier (trunk-maker)
bahutier.text: The bahutier makes wooden chests and trunks, storage and travel furniture very common before the wardrobe became standard, often reinforced with ironwork for travel.

baigneur.label: Baigneur
baigneur.summary: Keeper of, or employee at, a bathhouse.
baigneur.text: The baigneur keeps or works at a public bathhouse, an activity linked to personal hygiene before the private bathroom became common, these establishments sometimes also offering spa-type treatments.

baile.label: Baile
baile.summary: Local official exercising administrative and judicial functions, notably in the south of France.
baile.text: The baile (or bayle) is a local official exercising administrative and judicial functions on behalf of a lord or a community, particularly used in the south of France and Catalonia, a role related to that of the bailli in provinces under customary law.

bailli.label: Bailli (bailiff)
bailli.summary: Royal officer administering justice and government on the king's behalf in a bailiwick.
bailli.text: The bailli is a royal officer responsible for dispensing justice and administering a district (the bailliage) in the king's name, a key role in French territorial administration from the Middle Ages until the Revolution, which abolished bailliages in 1790.

baillive.label: Baillive
baillive.summary: Wife of a bailli, or a woman exercising comparable functions.
baillive.text: The baillive is the wife of a bailli, or, more rarely, a woman herself exercising administrative or judicial functions comparable to his in certain districts.

balaisier.label: Balaisier
balaisier.text: The balaisier makes brooms, generally from heather, broom-plant or birch twigs bound in a bundle around a handle, a trade often linked to heathland or forest areas that supplied the raw material.

balancier.label: Balancier (scale-maker)
balancier.text: The balancier makes and sells scales, weighing instruments essential to trade, whose manufacture required great mechanical precision to guarantee accurate measurement.

baleinier.label: Baleinier (whaler)
baleinier.text: The baleinier is a sailor aboard a ship engaged in whale hunting, an intense maritime activity from the 17th to the 19th century, notably for whale oil used in lighting before petroleum.

balliste.label: Balliste
balliste.summary: Soldier specialized in operating siege engines.
balliste.text: The balliste is a soldier specialized in operating war machines used to hurl projectiles — ballistas, catapults, trebuchets and other siege engines — a military role characteristic of Antiquity and the Middle Ages before gunpowder artillery.

balzmeister.label: Balzmeister
balzmeister.text: According to the glossary Les Métiers de nos Ancêtres, the balzmeister is an executioner practising in 16th-century Switzerland, a term of Germanic origin linked to this judicial function.

bambocheur.label: Bambocheur
bambocheur.summary: Term denoting a reveller, a habitual partygoer.
bambocheur.text: The bambocheur is one who "fait la bamboche", that is, leads a merry life and is a regular at feasts and revelry. More a character trait or a nickname noted with humour in some records than a genuine profession, the term does not correspond to any regulated trade.

bambrocheuse.label: Bambrocheuse
bambrocheuse.summary: Weaving-mill worker responsible for feeding the bobbins of the looms.
bambrocheuse.text: The bambrocheuse works in a cloth mill where she is responsible for feeding thread onto the bobbins of the looms, a preparatory task before weaving proper.

bandagiste.label: Bandagiste
bandagiste.summary: Maker of orthopaedic devices and trusses.
bandagiste.text: The bandagiste makes trusses, hernia belts and other orthopaedic devices, a medical and craft trade related to early orthopaedics, still practised today under the title of bandagiste-orthopédiste.

bandiste.label: Bandiste
bandiste.summary: Musician who is a member of a brass band or wind orchestra.
bandiste.text: The bandiste is a musician who is a member of a brass band or a wind orchestra ("band"), a role often held on a municipal or club basis in town bands and public festivities of the 19th and 20th centuries.

banquier.label: Banquier (banker)
banquier.summary: Professional managing deposits, loans and financial transactions.
banquier.text: The banquier manages money deposits, grants loans and carries out currency-exchange or financing transactions on behalf of individuals or businesses. The trade developed gradually from the medieval money-changer to the modern bank, with the rise of great banking houses in the 18th and 19th centuries.

baquetier.label: Baquetier
baquetier.summary: Craftsman making tubs and wooden vessels.
baquetier.text: The baquetier makes tubs, vats and other hooped wooden vessels, a craft close to coopering, essential for domestic, agricultural and industrial uses before the spread of plastic and metal.

baracanier.label: Baracanier
baracanier.summary: Maker of barracan, a coarse fabric of wool or goat hair.
baracanier.text: The baracanier makes barracan, a coarse fabric woven from wool or goat hair, used for hard-wearing, inexpensive clothing, a common textile product before the industrialization of weaving.

barasseur.label: Barasseur
barasseur.summary: Worker specialized in churning and making butter.
barasseur.text: The barasseur is a worker specialized in churning and making butter in dairies, an operation consisting of beating cream in a churn to separate the butter from the buttermilk.

barbaricaire.label: Barbaricaire
barbaricaire.summary: Embroiderer or tapestry-worker using gold thread and coloured silks.
barbaricaire.text: The barbaricaire is an embroiderer, worker or tapestry painter who uses gold thread and silks of various colours when depicting human and animal figures, a luxury craft intended for hangings and ceremonial garments.

barbier.label: Barbier (barber)
barbier.summary: Hair-cutter also performing minor surgical procedures.
barbier.text: The barbier shaves and cuts hair, but also performed, until the 18th century, minor surgical procedures (bloodletting, tooth extractions, small wounds), the trades of barber and surgeon not being formally separated in France until 1743.

barbier_perruquier.label: Barbier Perruquier (barber-wigmaker)
barbier_perruquier.summary: Barber also practising the trade of wigmaker.
barbier_perruquier.text: The barbier perruquier combined the two trades, commonly held together under the Ancien Régime: he shaved and dressed hair for his customers while also making wigs, before these professions separated in the 18th century.

bardeautier.label: Bardeautier (shingle-maker)
bardeautier.summary: Roofer making and laying wooden shingles.
bardeautier.text: The bardeautier makes and lays shingles, flat wooden roofing tiles split from timber, a traditional material in forested mountain regions before fired clay tile or slate became widespread.

bardeur.label: Bardeur
bardeur.summary: Porter carrying loads on his back or on a pack-frame.
bardeur.text: The bardeur carries loads on his back, often with the aid of a "barde" (a kind of pack-basket or saddle), a manual portering trade practised notably in ports, warehouses and quarries.

barillier.label: Barillier
barillier.summary: Maker of small barrels and casks.
barillier.text: The barillier makes small barrels and casks, a coopering craft specialized in small hooped containers for transporting and storing liquids or foodstuffs, attested under several regional spellings (barillar, barilleur, barillon).

barquer.label: Barquer
barquer.summary: Boatman carrying people or goods by boat.
barquer.text: The barquer pilots a boat to carry people or goods on a river or along a coast, a river or coastal boating trade common before the development of bridges and the railway.

barquier.label: Barquier
barquier.summary: Master of a boat ferrying between the port and moored ships, or a boatman on the Canal du Midi.
barquier.text: The barquier is the master of a boat or lighter making trips back and forth between the port and ships when the latter, owing to their draught, cannot dock directly; the term also denotes a boatman working the Canal du Midi.

barragiste.label: Barragiste
barragiste.summary: Person responsible for operating a dam or collecting a toll.
barragiste.text: The barragiste is responsible for operating a hydraulic structure (dam, lock) or for collecting a toll at a road or river barrier, depending on the precise sense attached to the term in the original record.

basse_contre.label: Basse-contre
basse_contre.summary: Singer with the lowest bass voice in the French choral tradition.
basse_contre.text: The basse-contre is the lowest voice in the French choral tradition, below the basse-taille, used notably in choir schools and church choirs under the Ancien Régime as well as in French Baroque opera.

basse_lissier.label: Basse-lissier (low-warp weaver)
basse_lissier.summary: Highly skilled weaver working on a low-warp loom to make tapestries and fine fabrics.
basse_lissier.text: The basse-lissier weaves on a horizontal loom (the "low warp"), a faster technique but considered less prestigious than high-warp weaving. He produces tapestries and fabrics of silk and wool, sometimes enhanced with gold and silver thread, depicting figures, animals and landscapes. The term is found notably in the records of clothmaking towns and tapestry centres such as Aubusson or Beauvais.

bassecourrier.label: Bassecourrier
bassecourrier.summary: Person responsible for tending and overseeing the farmyard (poultry, small livestock).
bassecourrier.text: The bassecourrier tends the farmyard of a farm or estate: raising and caring for poultry, rabbits and other small livestock. A modest rural term, it appears mainly in records concerning the staff of large farming estates.

batelier.label: Batelier (boatman)
batelier.summary: Boat operator carrying people and goods on inland waterways.
batelier.text: The batelier pilots a boat (barge, gabare, water coach) on rivers and canals, carrying goods and travellers before the rise of the railway. A very common trade in navigable valleys (Seine, Loire, Rhône) and one of the most frequent occupations in the records of river towns.

batier.label: Bâtier (pack-saddle maker)
batier.summary: Craftsman making pack-saddles, the load-carrying saddles placed on beasts of burden.
batier.text: The bâtier makes and repairs pack-saddles, wood and padded-leather devices placed on the backs of mules, donkeys and horses to carry loads. Close to the trades of saddler and harness-maker, it is attested mainly in mountain regions where pack-animal transport remained common.

batonnier.label: Bâtonnier
batonnier.summary: Elected head of a guild, or today, of a bar of lawyers.
batonnier.text: Under the Ancien Régime, the bâtonnier is the officer elected to head a confraternity or a trade guild, responsible for carrying its staff (an insignia) during processions and for presiding over its affairs. The term has survived to this day to denote the elected head of a bar of lawyers.

batteur.label: Batteur (thresher/beater)
batteur.summary: Worker carrying out beating work: grain, metals or various materials.
batteur.text: The batteur performs beating work, most often threshing grain with a flail before mechanization, but the term can also denote a worker beating iron, gold or other materials depending on the context of the record. Common in the countryside before mechanical threshers appeared in the 19th century.

batteur_d_archal.label: Batteur d'archal (wire-beater)
batteur_d_archal.summary: Worker who hammers brass or iron into thin sheets.
batteur_d_archal.text: The batteur d'archal hammers brass (or iron — "archal" originally denoted brass wire) into thin sheets, work related to that of the wire-drawer.

batteur_d_ecorces.label: Batteur d'écorces (bark-crusher)
batteur_d_ecorces.summary: Worker at a tan mill responsible for pulverizing oak bark used in leather-dressing.
batteur_d_ecorces.text: The batteur d'écorces works at a tan mill where he pulverizes oak bark used to produce tanbark, the tanning material used by leather-dressers and tanners.

batteur_d_etain.label: Batteur d'étain (tin-beater)
batteur_d_etain.summary: Worker who beats tin to reduce it to very thin sheets.
batteur_d_etain.text: The batteur d'étain hammers tin to reduce it to very thin sheets, used notably for making mirrors or decorative objects.

batteur_d_or.label: Batteur d'or (gold-beater)
batteur_d_or.summary: Specialized worker drawing and flattening gold (or silver) into very thin sheets.
batteur_d_or.text: The batteur d'or passes gold (or silver) wire or ingot through a rolling mill and then hammers it between pieces of goldbeater's skin to obtain extremely thin sheets, used in gilding, bookbinding or illumination. A skilled urban trade, organized into a guild in major cities such as Paris.

batteur_de_platre.label: Batteur de plâtre
batteur_de_platre.summary: Worker who crushes plaster before it is mixed.
batteur_de_platre.text: The batteur de plâtre crushes and grinds fired plaster before it is mixed and slaked for use.

batteur_en_grange.label: Batteur en grange (barn thresher)
batteur_en_grange.summary: Farm worker threshing grain with a flail in the barn after harvest.
batteur_en_grange.text: The batteur en grange threshes sheaves of wheat, rye or oats with a flail inside the barn, separating the grain from the straw. Seasonal and arduous work, it employed many rural day-labourers before mechanical threshers spread in the 19th century.

baudelier.label: Baudelier
baudelier.summary: Craftsman making baldrics, straps and leather belts.
baudelier.text: The baudelier makes baldrics and leather straps used to carry swords, horns or loads. Close to the saddler and harness-maker, this leather trade is attested mainly in towns with military or transport activity.

baudroyer.label: Baudroyer (leather currier)
baudroyer.summary: Leather craftsman specialized in currying (softening and finishing tanned hides).
baudroyer.text: The baudroyer prepares and softens leather that has already been tanned — an operation called currying — to make it supple and usable by saddlers, shoemakers and harness-makers. The term, from "baudroyerie", an old word for currying, is found in the records of towns with a tanning tradition.

baudrucheur.label: Baudrucheur
baudrucheur.summary: Gold-beater who reduces gold to leaf between two pieces of goldbeater's skin.
baudrucheur.text: The baudrucheur is a worker specialized in gold-beating, who interposes pieces of goldbeater's skin (treated ox gut) between the metal leaves to thin them without tearing them while hammering. A trade ancillary to that of the gold-beater, working in the same specialized urban workshops.

baugeur.label: Baugeur (cob-builder)
baugeur.summary: Building worker working with "bauge", a mix of earth and straw used in construction.
baugeur.text: The baugeur builds walls out of bauge, a mix of clay-rich earth, water and straw pressed by hand or in rammed layers, a traditional technique in regions without readily available stone (Normandy, Anjou). The trade is close to that of the bousilleur, who uses cob on a wattle frame.

bayle.label: Bayle
bayle.summary: Local official exercising administrative and judicial functions on behalf of a lord or community.
bayle.text: The bayle (or baile) is, in the south of France and Occitan-speaking areas, a seigneurial or communal official responsible for minor justice, policing and the administration of seigneurial dues in a locality. It corresponds roughly to the bailli of the north, but remains a more modest local title, common in Provence, Languedoc and Roussillon.

bazardier.label: Bazardier
bazardier.summary: Merchant keeping a bazaar, a shop selling assorted goods.
bazardier.text: The bazardier keeps a bazaar, a retail shop offering assorted items (haberdashery, trinkets, sundries). The term, of Persian origin via Arabic, spread in French from the 19th century onward with the rise of department stores and eponymous shops.

becheur.label: Bêcheur (digger)
becheur.summary: Farm worker turning over the soil with a spade.
becheur.text: The bêcheur works the soil with a spade, arduous manual work used notably in gardens, vineyards or small plots where a plough cannot be used. A common countryside term before mechanization.

becheux.label: Bêcheux
becheux.summary: Worker digging clay for use in tile and brick works.
becheux.text: The bêcheux digs, with a spade, the clay used in tile and brick works, a preparatory task before the shaping of tiles and bricks.

bedeau.label: Bedeau (beadle)
bedeau.summary: Lay employee of a parish responsible for order and the practical running of ceremonies.
bedeau.text: The bedeau is a layman in the service of a parish church, responsible for keeping order during services, ringing the bells, opening the doors and assisting the clergy with practical tasks. A familiar figure in parish records, he often also held other minor communal offices (gravedigger, town crier).

belandrier.label: Bélandrier
belandrier.summary: Sailor or boatman operating a bélandre, a small sailing boat used for coastal trade.
belandrier.text: The bélandrier sails aboard a bélandre, a flat-bottomed sailing boat used for coastal and river transport, notably in the north of France and Flanders. A trade close to that of the boatman, but tied to a specific type of vessel.

benatier.label: Bénatier
benatier.summary: Craftsman making, or user of, bénatons, willow baskets or packframes used for carrying.
benatier.text: The bénatier makes or uses bénatons — large baskets or pack-frames woven from willow — used notably to carry the grape harvest or other crops on a man's or a mule's back, a practice well attested in the Massif Central. The term is sometimes mistakenly confused with "bénéficier" owing to their similar spelling, but denotes a distinct craft or peasant trade.

beneficier.label: Bénéficier
beneficier.summary: Cleric holding an ecclesiastical benefice, income attached to a religious office.
beneficier.text: The bénéficier is a cleric who holds an ecclesiastical benefice: an office (parish, chapel, prebend) with land revenues or annuities granted by the Church. He does not necessarily perform an active pastoral role and may hold several benefices at once, a common practice under the Ancien Régime before the Tridentine and revolutionary reforms.

benoit.label: Benoit
benoit.summary: In the Landes, a beadle responsible for the upkeep and manual work of a church.
benoit.text: In the Landes, the benoit is a beadle responsible for the upkeep and material work of a church's fabric (vestry).

berger.label: Berger (shepherd)
berger.summary: Keeper of flocks, most often sheep, driven out to pasture.
berger.text: The berger keeps and drives a flock, mainly sheep, to pasture, watching over its protection and breeding. One of the oldest and most frequent rural occupations in parish records, he could be employed by a village community or a large landowner.

berlingier.label: Berlingier
berlingier.summary: Weaver making berlinge, a coarse fabric of thread and wool, in Brittany.
berlingier.text: In Brittany, the berlingier weaves berlinge, a fairly thick fabric mixing thread (linen or hemp) with wool, used for hard-wearing clothing and linen. The same fabric is called "casto" in other regions, where the corresponding weaver is known as a castotier.

besocheur.label: Besocheur
besocheur.summary: Farm worker turning over the soil with a besoche, a heavy long-handled spade.
besocheur.text: The besocheur works the soil with a besoche, a tool similar to a spade but wider and heavier, used notably in western France (Poitou, Vendée) for manual digging on ground unworkable with a plough.

bibelotier.label: Bibelotier
bibelotier.summary: Merchant selling bibelots, small decorative or curio objects.
bibelotier.text: The bibelotier sells bibelots — small decorative, curio or inexpensive objects — in a shop or at markets. The term spread especially in the 19th century with the bourgeois taste for ornamental objects.

billardier.label: Billardier
billardier.summary: Maker of billiard tables and other game tables.
billardier.text: The billardier makes billiard tables and other game tables, a trade that developed mainly from the 18th century onward with the vogue for billiards in cafés and clubs.

billonneur.label: Billonneur
billonneur.summary: Money-changer specialized in sorting and exchanging billon coinage, a base alloy poor in precious metal.
billonneur.text: The billonneur is a money-changer specialized in identifying and exchanging billon coinage — a low-gold or low-silver alloy — and worn or debased coins. This modest financial trade played a useful role at a time when many coins of unequal quality circulated at once.

bilotier.label: Bilotier
bilotier.summary: In the Brie region, a goose-keeper.
bilotier.text: The bilotier is, in the Brie region, the keeper of a flock of geese, driving them to pasture and watching over them, a minor pastoral activity comparable to that of the shepherd with sheep.

bineur.label: Bineur
bineur.summary: Farm worker hoeing crops, that is, loosening the soil and pulling up weeds.
bineur.text: The bineur carries out hoeing, an operation that loosens the surface soil between rows of crops (vines, vegetables) while removing weeds. Frequent seasonal work, often done by day-labourers.

biscayeur.label: Biscayeur
biscayeur.summary: Comb-maker who unrolls animal horn to turn it into a flat, usable material.
biscayeur.text: The biscayeur is a comb-making worker who treats animal horn, unrolling and flattening it under heat to make a flat material used in the manufacture of combs and other small objects. A specialized technical step in horn-working.

bisettiere.label: Bisettière
bisettiere.summary: Female worker making bisette, a coarse, inexpensive lace.
